session.question: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?
session.answer:
The ClinicalTrials.gov record describes DECISION as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III trial in patients with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer. Treatment was continued until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent. Efficacy assessments were performed every 56 days, and safety assessments were performed every 28 days for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter. After progression, patients could cross over to sorafenib at investigator discretion. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)

The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), time to progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetics. The trial registration identifier was NCT00984282. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)

pqac-a586d08b: The provided excerpt is a 2023 phase II randomized placebo-controlled trial of risankizumab for hidradenitis suppurativa, not a description of the DECISION phase III study. It reports that patients with moderate-to-severe HS were randomized 1:1:1 to risankizumab 180 mg, risankizumab 360 mg, or placebo at weeks 0, 1, 2, 4, and 12; placebo patients later received blinded risankizumab 360 mg at weeks 16, 17, and 18, and all patients then received open-label 360 mg every 8 weeks from weeks 20–60. The primary endpoint was HiSCR at week 16, and the trial registration listed is NCT03926169.
From Alexa B. Kimball, Errol P. Prens, Thierry Passeron, Emanual Maverakis, Irina Turchin, Stefan Beeck, Leonidas Drogaris, Ziqian Geng, Tianyu Zhan, Izabella Messina, and Falk G. Bechara. pqac-5498a024: The excerpt is about the CheckPRO phase II trial and does not mention the DECISION phase III study. It describes an open-label, randomized, two-stage phase II design in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, with 80 evaluable patients receiving four cycles of ipilimumab/nivolumab with or without SBRT (24 Gy in 3 fractions) followed by 10 cycles of nivolumab. Co-primary endpoints are objective response rate and PSA response rate; secondary endpoints include safety, radiographic PFS, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, PSA-PFS beyond 12 weeks, quality of life, and overall survival. Trial registration listed: EudraCT 2018-003461-34 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05655715.
From Nicklas Juel Spindler, Gitte Fredberg Persson, Susann Theile, Dorte Lisbeth Nielsen, Estrid V Høgdall, Gina Al-Farra, Helle Westergren Hendel, Torben Lorentzen, Inge Marie Svane, Henriette Lindberg, and Rikke Løvendahl Eefsen. contexts.context: The excerpt describes a phase 1 study of RO7297089 in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, not the DECISION phase III study. It reports weekly intravenous infusion dosing, starting at 60 mg, with 27 patients treated between 60 and 1850 mg. The maximum tolerated dose was not reached. Common adverse events included anemia, infusion-related reaction, and thrombocytopenia; common grade ≥3 toxicities were ALT/AST increase and reduced lymphocyte count. Pharmacokinetics suggested non-linear behavior and target-mediated drug disposition. Trial registration for this phase 1 study was ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04434469, registered June 16, 2020.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: What does the ClinicalTrials.gov record say about the DECISION phase III study design, treatment schedule, endpoints, and trial registration identifier?

The ClinicalTrials.gov record describes DECISION as a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled phase III trial in patients with locally advanced or metastatic radioactive iodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer. Treatment was continued until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxicity, noncompliance, or withdrawal of consent. Efficacy assessments were performed every 56 days, and safety assessments were performed every 28 days for the first 8 months and every 56 days thereafter. After progression, patients could cross over to sorafenib at investigator discretion. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)

The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), time to progression, disease control rate, response rate, duration of response, safety, and pharmacokinetics. The trial registration identifier was NCT00984282. (brose2011rationaleanddesign chunk 1)
